![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262816/assets/0ea627b0f4b68b4cde9c6ae07ceafcba35007556202ff5bf9a7981dee0ce5a7a.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{12}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{12}{5}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{12}{5} & =\frac{10x+4}{6x-2} \\ 12(6x-2) & =5(10x+4) \\ 72x-24 & =50x+20 \\ 22x & =44 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =10x+4=10(2)+4=24, \\ AC & =6x-2=6(2)-2=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\cdot 24 \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$
